subproblem.title: Dilation change of variables for H^n set integrals over blow-up images η_{x,r}(M)
subproblem.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ, x ∈ ℝ^N (= Euclidean N) and r > 0. Let M ⊆ ℝ^N be an arbitrary set and F : ℝ^N → ℝ an arbitrary function. Let η := Chapter03.blowUpMap x r, so η(y) = r⁻¹ • (y − x), and let H^n := μHE[n]. Then ∫_{η(M)} F dH^n = r⁻¹^n · ∫_M F(η(z)) dH^n(z), as Bochner set integrals; no measurability or integrability is assumed of M or F.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (x : Euclidean N) (r : ℝ) (M : Set (Euclidean N)) (F : Euclidean N → ℝ), 0 < r → ∫ y in Chapter03.blowUpMap x r '' M, F y ∂μHE[n] = r⁻¹ ^ n * ∫ z in M, F (Chapter03.blowUpMap x r z) ∂μHE[n]
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Step 3 of the supplied proof of frt_weighted_approx_tangent (the homothety change of variables), with full details and for arbitrary M and F.

Notation: H := μHE[n]; η := Chapter03.blowUpMap x r, so η(y) = r⁻¹ • (y − x) (the definition unfolds by rfl); ψ(y) := x + r • y. All integrals are Bochner integrals, and nothing is assumed about M or F.

1. η is a homeomorphism of ℝ^N with inverse ψ. Since r ≠ 0, ψ(η(y)) = x + r • (r⁻¹ • (y − x)) = x + (y − x) = y and η(ψ(y)) = r⁻¹ • ((x + r • y) − x) = r⁻¹ • (r • y) = y. Both maps are continuous, being built from translations and scalings. Consequently η is a measurable embedding (Homeomorph.measurableEmbedding) and is injective.

2. Scaling of H under η⁻¹. Let S ⊆ ℝ^N be any set, not necessarily measurable. Since ψ inverts η, η⁻¹(S) = ψ(S) = τ(r • S), where τ(y) := x + y and r • S := {r • s : s ∈ S}. τ is an isometry (isometry_add_left), so H(τ(r • S)) = H(r • S) (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image). Since r ≠ 0, H(r • S) = ‖r‖₊^n • H(S) (Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀). As r > 0, the [0, ∞]-valued factor ‖r‖₊^n equals ENNReal.ofReal(r)^n = ENNReal.ofReal(r^n). Therefore H(η⁻¹(S)) = ENNReal.ofReal(r^n) · H(S).

3. Pushforward of H. For every Borel S, (H.map η)(S) = H(η⁻¹(S)) (Measure.map_apply; η is continuous, hence measurable), which equals ENNReal.ofReal(r^n) · H(S) = (ENNReal.ofReal(r^n) • H)(S) by Step 2. By Measure.ext, H.map η = ENNReal.ofReal(r^n) • H.

4. Pushforward of H⌞M. Since η is a measurable embedding, MeasurableEmbedding.restrict_map gives (H.map η).restrict (η(M)) = (H.restrict (η⁻¹(η(M)))).map η, and η⁻¹(η(M)) = M by injectivity. Combining this with Step 3 and Measure.restrict_smul: (H.restrict M).map η = (H.map η).restrict (η(M)) = (ENNReal.ofReal(r^n) • H).restrict (η(M)) = ENNReal.ofReal(r^n) • H.restrict (η(M)).

5. Change of variables. Because η is a measurable embedding, ∫ G d(ν.map η) = ∫ G(η(z)) dν(z) for every measure ν and every function G : ℝ^N → ℝ (MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map; no measurability of G is needed). Take ν := H.restrict M and G := F, then use Step 4 and integral_smul_measure (∫ G d(c • ν') = c.toReal · ∫ G dν'): ∫_M F(η(z)) dH(z) = ∫ F d((H.restrict M).map η) = (ENNReal.ofReal(r^n)).toReal · ∫_{η(M)} F dH = r^n · ∫_{η(M)} F dH. The last step is ENNReal.toReal_ofReal, using r^n ≥ 0.

6. Since r⁻¹^n · r^n = (r⁻¹ · r)^n = 1, multiplying the identity of Step 5 by r⁻¹^n gives r⁻¹^n · ∫_M F(η(z)) dH(z) = ∫_{η(M)} F dH. Here η(M) = Chapter03.blowUpMap x r '' M and F(η(z)) = F (Chapter03.blowUpMap x r z), so this is exactly the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: η = blowUpMap x r is a homeomorphism with inverse y ↦ x + r • y, hence an injective measurable embedding.
For every set S, H^n(η⁻¹ S) = H^n(x + r • S) = r^n H^n(S) (translation isometry and Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀).
H^n.map η = ENNReal.ofReal(r^n) • H^n (Measure.ext on Borel sets).
(H^n⌞M).map η = ENNReal.ofReal(r^n) • H^n⌞η(M) (MeasurableEmbedding.restrict_map, η⁻¹(η M) = M, Measure.restrict_smul).
MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map and integral_smul_measure give ∫_M F∘η dH^n = r^n ∫_{η(M)} F dH^n; multiply by r⁻¹^n.

audit.reason: The one-line Lean proposition exactly matches the prose, including arbitrary M and F and the hypothesis r > 0. The supplied inverse establishes a homeomorphism; Hausdorff scaling gives the pushforward factor r^n; measurable-embedding restriction and integral transport require no measurability of M or F; cancellation gives precisely r⁻¹ ^ n. All six steps are complete and non-circular. The bare name is unreserved, and the frozen type elaborates independently. No problematic matrix-unit construction occurs.

subproblem.title: Integration against a measure represented as θ·H^n⌞M on Borel sets, for integrands vanishing off a Borel set
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclidean N)) (M K : Set (Euclidean N)) (θ h : Euclidean N → ℝ), NullMeasurableSet M μHE[n] → (∀ y ∈ M, 0 < θ y) → MeasurableSet K → IntegrableOn θ (M ∩ K) μHE[n] → (∀ B : Set (Euclidean N), MeasurableSet B → μ B = ∫⁻ y in B ∩ M, ENNReal.ofReal (θ y) ∂μHE[n]) → (∀ z, z ∉ K → h z = 0) → ∫ z, h z ∂μ = ∫ z in M, h z * θ z ∂μHE[n]
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Step 2 of the supplied proof of frt_weighted_approx_tangent (Simon Ch. 8, Thm 1.2, step 7: μ_V restricted to compact pieces is the weighted Hausdorff measure θ H^n⌞M), together with the support reduction ∫_M = ∫_{M ∩ K'} used in its Step 4. Here it is stated for an arbitrary measure μ, a Borel set K and an arbitrary integrand h.

Notation: H := μHE[n]; ν := H.restrict (M ∩ K) (= H⌞(M ∩ K)); ρ(y) := ENNReal.ofReal (θ y) ∈ [0, ∞).

Every integral of a real function is a Bochner integral, which is 0 for non-integrable integrands. Each identity used below holds for arbitrary integrands, so no measurability, boundedness or integrability of h is needed. (In the parent's Step 2 the boundedness and Borel hypotheses on h only served to note that both sides are integrable.)

1. μ.restrict K = ν.withDensity ρ. Two measures on the Borel σ-algebra of ℝ^N are equal as soon as they agree on every Borel set (Measure.ext). Let B be Borel; since K is Borel, so is B ∩ K. Then (μ.restrict K)(B) = μ(B ∩ K) (Measure.restrict_apply, B measurable) = ∫⁻_{(B ∩ K) ∩ M} ρ dH (hypothesis applied to the Borel set B ∩ K). On the other side, (ν.withDensity ρ)(B) = ∫⁻_B ρ dν (withDensity_apply, B measurable) = ∫⁻ ρ d(H.restrict (B ∩ (M ∩ K))) (Measure.restrict_restrict, B measurable). Since (B ∩ K) ∩ M = B ∩ (M ∩ K), the two values are equal.

2. Localization. Because h(z) = 0 for every z ∉ K, h equals its indicator 1_K·h. Hence ∫ h dμ = ∫_K h dμ = ∫ h d(μ.restrict K) (setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero, which needs no measurability).

3. Density formula. IntegrableOn θ (M ∩ K) H means θ is ν-integrable, so θ is ν-a.e. strongly measurable and hence ν-a.e. measurable. Therefore ρ = ENNReal.ofReal ∘ θ is ν-a.e. measurable (AEMeasurable.ennreal_ofReal), and ρ(y) < ∞ for every y. For such a density, every g : ℝ^N → ℝ satisfies ∫ g d(ν.withDensity ρ) = ∫ ρ(y).toReal · g(y) dν(y) (integral_withDensity_eq_integral_toReal_smul₀). Indeed g is integrable for ν.withDensity ρ iff ρ.toReal·g is integrable for ν, in which case this is the usual density formula; otherwise both sides are 0. Taking g := h and using Step 1: ∫ h d(μ.restrict K) = ∫ ρ(y).toReal · h(y) dν(y).

4. Removing the density. M ∩ K is H-null-measurable, as the intersection of the H-null-measurable set M with the Borel set K. Hence ν-a.e. y lies in M ∩ K (ae_restrict_mem₀). For such y, θ(y) > 0 by hypothesis, so ρ(y).toReal = (ENNReal.ofReal θ(y)).toReal = θ(y) (ENNReal.toReal_ofReal) and ρ(y).toReal · h(y) = h(y) θ(y). By integral_congr_ae, ∫ ρ.toReal · h dν = ∫_{M ∩ K} h(z) θ(z) dH(z).

5. From M ∩ K to M. Put g := h·θ. The set M is the disjoint union of the H-null-measurable sets M ∩ K and M \ K, and g vanishes identically on M \ K because h does. Hence g is integrable on M iff it is integrable on M ∩ K, and in that case ∫_M g dH = ∫_{M ∩ K} g dH + ∫_{M \ K} g dH = ∫_{M ∩ K} g dH. If g is not integrable on either set, both set integrals are 0. Either way ∫_M h θ dH = ∫_{M ∩ K} h θ dH (setIntegral_eq_of_subset_of_ae_sdiff_eq_zero with the null-measurable set M, M ∩ K ⊆ M, and g = 0 on M \ (M ∩ K)).

6. Chaining Steps 2, 3, 4 and 5: ∫ h dμ = ∫ h d(μ.restrict K) = ∫ ρ.toReal · h dν = ∫_{M ∩ K} h θ dH = ∫_M h θ dH. ∎
proof_key_steps: μ.restrict K = (μHE[n].restrict (M ∩ K)).withDensity (ENNReal.ofReal ∘ θ): compare the two measures on each Borel B, using the hypothesis for the Borel set B ∩ K together with withDensity_apply and Measure.restrict_restrict.
∫ h dμ = ∫ h d(μ.restrict K) because h = 0 off K (setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero).
integral_withDensity_eq_integral_toReal_smul₀ (ENNReal.ofReal ∘ θ is a.e. measurable because θ is integrable on M ∩ K, and it is finite): ∫ h d(μ.restrict K) = ∫ (ofReal θ).toReal · h d(H^n⌞(M ∩ K)).
A.e. on the null-measurable set M ∩ K, (ofReal θ).toReal = θ since θ > 0 on M; hence the integral equals ∫_{M ∩ K} h θ dH^n.
h θ = 0 on M \ K and M is null-measurable, so ∫_{M ∩ K} h θ dH^n = ∫_M h θ dH^n (setIntegral_eq_of_subset_of_ae_sdiff_eq_zero).
